diagnostic_evidence.quote: (for $n_2$ large enough so that $\varepsilon-\frac1{n_2}>0$; for finitely many small $n_2$ define the output arbitrarily in $\mathcal{M}_H$)

issues.failure_explanation: For small n_1 the Riemann-sum seminorm may vanish identically on V_{n_2} (e.g. a coarse quadrature whose nodes are common zeros of V_{n_2}), so the constraint set {g in V_{n_2}: ||g||^RS_{n_1}=1} is empty and h_{n_2,n_1} (hence the output Gamma_{n_2,n_1}) is undefined or empty, and therefore not an element of M_H; likewise the ratio argument in Step 3(b) needs denominators bounded away from 0, which only holds for large n_1. The source patches only 'finitely many small n_2', which does not cover the n_1 direction. The tower of general algorithms is thus not defined as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Stipulate arbitrary fixed outputs in M_H also for the (finitely many, per fixed n_2) pairs (n_2,n_1) where the RS constraint set is empty or the threshold set is empty; a content-free degenerate-case assignment.
issues.overall_effect: The base-level algorithms in Steps 3-4 of the meta-theorem are not well-defined on degenerate index pairs; all convergence statements (n_1 to infinity, then n_2 to infinity) are unaffected once arbitrary outputs are assigned there.
issues.title: Base-level discrete residual is ill-defined for small quadrature index
issues.why_classification: A local degenerate-case patch with a single forced choice; the method, the SCI bounds, and the advertised scope all survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: such that every Borel function $\varphi:\X\to\C$ is represented by some code $c$ with $\varphi=\varphi_c$.

issues.failure_explanation: No such coding exists. If Code were Polish, ev Borel, and every Borel function represented, then for the uncountable Polish X fix a Borel isomorphism beta: Code -> X (uncountable standard Borel spaces are isomorphic); the map d(x) := ev(beta^{-1}(x), x) + 1 is Borel, hence has a code c*, and at x* = beta(c*) one gets ev(c*,x*) = d(x*) = ev(c*,x*) + 1, a contradiction. (This is also why a Borel set universal for all Borel sets cannot exist.) The parenthetical 'code Borel sets and then code Borel functions' is exactly the impossible step. Thus the entire subsequent verification that B is Borel is unfounded as written.

failure_location.quote: there exists a Polish space of \textit{codes} $\mathsf{Code}(\X,\C)$ and a \textit{Borel evaluation map}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the impossible coding by the standard Polish witness space: the unit ball of L^infty(omega) with the weak-* topology (compact metrizable since L^1 is separable), take P = (ball(L^infty))^N, express the norm constraints via countably many L^1 test integrals, and use joint Borelness of (F,f) -> f o F via separate continuity; then B is Borel and A_{z_0} = proj(B) is analytic. A contained but nontrivial recoding argument; the lemma's statement is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of analyticity of A_{z_0} collapses as written; Step 1 of thm:route-IF-to-Az0 (Sigma^1_1 upper bound) and hence the completeness/non-Borelness conclusion and thm:SCI_A_infty_Linfty_decision lose their support (independently of ISSUE-005).
issues.title: Analyticity proof rests on a nonexistent Borel coding of all Borel functions
issues.why_classification: The proof's key premise is false and must be replaced by a different coding construction with a measurability re-verification (a contained new argument), but the lemma's conclusion and all dependent statements survive without weakening.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The rule $[f] \mapsto [f\circ F]$ defines a well-defined linear operator
$F$ is nonsingular with respect to $\omega$, i.e.\ $F_{\#}\omega\ll \omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: By prop:boundednessLoo, [f] -> [f o F] is well-defined on L^infty classes only if F is nonsingular. The lemma assumes only a measurable L-cycle structure with F^L = id pointwise; such a map can be singular (e.g. an involution of [0,1] swapping a null set with a positive-measure set of the same cardinality), in which case the operator K_F the lemma speaks about does not exist on L^infty(Z,nu). The statement as given is false without the hypothesis F_# nu << nu.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis 'F is nonsingular' to the lemma; all current applications already satisfy it.
issues.overall_effect: None beyond the lemma itself: every application in the paper (finite permutations of equal-measure cylinders, measure-preserving homeomorphisms) is nonsingular, so the uses are unaffected.
issues.title: Cycle-spectrum lemma omits the nonsingularity needed for the L^infty Koopman operator to exist
issues.why_classification: A single standard local condition must be added; no application, method, or conclusion changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: be a measurable partition such that $0<\omega(\mathcal X_j)<\infty$ for all $j$.
and let $\omega$ be the $(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$-Bernoulli product probability measure on $X$.

issues.failure_explanation: lem:Linfty-block-sap assumes every block satisfies 0 < omega(X_j), but the block {x_infty} has measure 0 under the (1/2,1/2)-Bernoulli product measure. The same hypothesis violation occurs in lem:spectrum_FS (same partition) and can occur in lem:transfer-cantor (X minus Y may be null). The conclusion is nonetheless unaffected: L^infty of a null block is the zero space and contributes nothing to the product or to the union, and the value {1} attributed to the identity on {x_infty} is already contained in every U_{2^{k_m}}.

failure_location.quote: Thus we may apply the $L^\infty$ block-decomposition \cref{lem:Linfty-block-sap} to the measurable partition

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate lem:Linfty-block-sap allowing null blocks (they contribute the zero summand and are omitted from the union), or drop {x_infty} from the partition; the 'contributes {1}' remark for the null block should be deleted (1 is in the union anyway).
issues.overall_effect: A hypothesis of the invoked block lemma is violated at three application sites; the spectral formulas obtained are correct after a trivial adjustment, so no downstream content changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
choose $u_m(S)$ to be the $\prec$-least extension $v$ such that
\[
\Sigma(v)\ \subseteq\ S\cap 2^m.
\]

S\in\mathcal V
\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists\ A\subseteq\omega\text{ coinfinite},\ \exists x\in 2^\omega\ \ \text{s.t.}\ \ S_{A,x}\subseteq S.

issues.failure_explanation: The greedy (= lexicographically least admissible) pattern need not maximize the star count. Counterexample built from the source's own definitions: let S be the union of the Silver tree S_{A,x} with A = {0}, x(0) = 0 (all strings with first bit 0; A is coinfinite, so S in V) and the single branch 10^omega (and its prefixes). At level 1 both strings 0 and 1 are in S, so the greedy rule stars: u_1 = *. At every level m >= 2 the star extension is blocked by the string 10^{m-2}1 (not in S), while the 0 extension works, so u_m(S) = *0^{m-1} and k_m(S) = 1 for all m, although the Silver witness w_m has |m minus A| = m-1 stars. Consequently |P_m(S)| = 2 on every Y_m and all remaining orbits are dump 2-cycles or fixed points, so F_S^2 = id, hence K_{F_S}^2 = Id and (by the resolvent identity of lem:cycle-spectrum Step 2) sigma_ap(K_{F_S}) is contained in {+1,-1}. Thus z_0 is not in sigma_ap(K_{Psi(S)}) although S is in V: the forward implication, and hence the equivalence cor:SilverKoopman_equivalence, is false for the construction. Moreover the failure is structural: the construction's z_0-fiber equals {S: sup_m k_m(S) = infinity}, which is a G_delta (Borel) set whenever k_m(S) depends only on S restricted to level m, whereas V is non-Borel, so no repair that keeps finitely-determined cycle data can realize the claimed equivalence.

failure_location.quote: By the star-priority construction of $u_m(S)$ (it chooses $\ast$ whenever that choice preserves $\Sigma(\cdot)\subseteq S\cap 2^m$), the pattern $u_m(S)$ has at least as many $\ast$-coordinates as any admissible witness pattern.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the star-priority rule in def:star-priority-um by a selection producing nested admissible patterns with unbounded star count exactly when S is in V, re-prove both directions of the equivalence (and port it to def:Psi-Lip), and change the gadget so that sigma_ap(K_{F_S}) is not a Borel function of finitely-determined cycle data, since otherwise the z_0-fiber remains Borel and cannot coincide with the non-Borel V.
issues.overall_effect: The dynamical back end of both headline lower-bound results is broken: the equivalence eq:SilverApKoopEquiv fails, so the Borel reduction IF_omega <=_B A_{z_0} (thm:route-IF-to-Az0) does not reduce correctly, the Sigma^1_1-completeness of A_{z_0} and SCI_A = infinity (thm:SCI_A_infty_Linfty_decision) lose their proof, and the type-G argument collapses: in the proof of thm:SCI_G_infty_mclasses the fiber Phi^{-1}(C_{z_0}) is the Borel set {S: sup k_m = infinity} rather than the non-Borel V, so no contradiction arises (the same defect propagates to cor:SCI_G_infty_alpha via the 1-Lipschitz variant def:Psi-Lip, which uses the same u_m(S)). The abstract/intro announcements of these results are consequences of the same root.
issues.title: Greedy star-priority witness fails: the forward Silver-tree/Koopman implication is false
issues.why_classification: The central reduction of the paper is false as written (explicit counterexample), both flagship theorems (type-A analytic completeness/SCI_A = infinity and type-G SCI_G = infinity) are abandoned as proved, and every supported resolution requires an essentially new dynamical construction rather than a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For $\omega\in\Omega$ we have $f(\omega)\in B(y,r)$ iff there exists $m$ such that
$f(\omega)\in B(y,r)^{(m)}$ and then eventually $f_n(\omega)\in B(y,r)^{(m)}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed set identity is false: f_n(omega) eventually in the open 2^{-m}-neighborhood B(y,r)^{(m)} only yields d(f(omega),y) <= r + 2^{-m}, so the right-hand side also contains points whose limit lies on or just outside the boundary of B(y,r). Concrete counterexample: the constant sequence f_n = z with d(z,y) = r + 2^{-(m+1)} belongs to every f_n^{-1}(B(y,r)^{(m)}) but z is not in B(y,r). The lemma's statement (pointwise limits of Borel maps into metric spaces are Borel) is true; the standard correct identity uses closed sub-balls of radius r - 2^{-m}: f(omega) in B(y,r) iff exists m such that eventually f_n(omega) is in the closed ball of radius r - 2^{-m}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace B(y,r)^{(m)} by closed balls of radius r - 2^{-m} in the displayed identity; the rest of the proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The induction in thm:borel_tower_implies_borel_target invokes this false identity at every limit step; once the routine correction is made, that theorem and its later use in the type-G argument stand (the type-G theorem fails anyway for the independent reason in ISSUE-005).
issues.title: False neighborhood identity in the proof that pointwise limits of Borel maps are Borel
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction to a proof display with the standard forced fix; the lemma's conclusion and all downstream statements survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The last inference is invalid for general block operators: residuals sigma_inf(T_{j(n)} - lambda) -> 0 do not imply dist(lambda, union_j sigma_ap(T_j)) -> 0. Counterexample to the general principle: for the n-by-n nilpotent Jordan blocks J_n one has sigma_inf(J_n - lambda) of order |lambda|^n -> 0 for every fixed |lambda| < 1, while sigma_ap(J_n) = {0} for all n; hence every |lambda| < 1 is an approximate eigenvalue of the l^infinity-direct sum, yet the closure of the union of block spectra is {0}. The proof uses nothing Koopman-specific, so part (iii) is unproved at its stated generality (arbitrary nonsingular F and arbitrary invariant measurable partition), and no estimate relating dist(lambda, sigma_ap(block)) to the block residual is supplied.

failure_location.quote:
Thus $\lambda$ is an approximate eigenvalue of the operator $\K_{F|_{\mathcal X_{j(n)}}}$ along the sequence $j(n)$,
which exactly means $\lambda$ belongs to the closure of $\bigcup_j\sigma_{\mathrm{ap}}(\K_{F|_{\mathcal X_j}})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the lemma to the block types actually used (finite permutations of equal-measure cylinders, identity blocks, invertible isometries) and prove for those a blockwise estimate dist(lambda, spec(block)) <= C * sigma_inf(block - lambda) with a universal constant C: the blocks are isometries, and for an L-cycle both sigma_inf and the distance to L-th roots are controlled by |1 - lambda^L| with uniform constants. This is a contained nontrivial computation; alternatively, prove the union formula for arbitrary Koopman blocks by a new argument.
issues.overall_effect: The upper-bound half of the block-union formula is unsupported; every spectral computation that routes through it (the spectrum formula for F_S in both gadget versions, the clopen-subsystem transfer, the perturbation-gap lemma, and the results built on them) inherits the gap as written.
issues.title: Invalid inference in the union formula for the approximate point spectrum of an l^infty block product
issues.why_classification: A necessary nontrivial step is missing and the stated generality is unsupported, but a contained estimate valid for all block types in the paper repairs the lemma and leaves every application unchanged.
